 Re-ranking 138 college football teams after Week 11: Carnage in the back half of the top 25
 By Chris Vannini Nov. 16, 2026 6:00 am EST Updated Share article 241 Are you sure you want a 24-team College Football Playoff? Do you realize what kinds of teams will make the field?
 I don’t mean you, the fan. Polling data already showed fans don’t want it. I mean you, the conference commissioners, stewards of this sport, all of whom supported a 24-team field because it would get more of your members in the field. This week’s rankings show just how far down the barrel the committee will have to dig for teams.
 Advertisement
 It was an odd weekend. The top 12 teams in last week’s Athletic 138 all won, and 18 of the next 24 lost.
 As a result, several teams with 6-4 records are in the top 25 this week. Somebody has to be. We might get 7-5 teams in the first 24-team CFP next year. The SEC hasn’t even gotten to that ninth conference game yet, which will add an extra loss to half the league’s teams.
 The committee has it easy this week. You can debate the order of the top 12, but who is in the top 12 is pretty simple. It’s the rest that will be a struggle, and it’s the rest that the committee will have to take more seriously next year. In a 24-team CFP world, they’ll probably have to rank 30 or 35 teams, and they know it.
 How Texas saved its season in Death Valley Ralph D. Russo Picking between teams full of flaws will be tough. But of course, that’s why we do it here every week, if the committee needs any help. Here is this week’s edition of The Athletic 138.
 The only change here is Indiana sliding up one spot. The Hoosiers beat USC 27-13, a much-needed quality win. None of the other wins were notable enough to move anyone ahead or below someone else.
 Texas Tech stays at No. 11 despite an impressive 52-27 win at Oklahoma State, only because everyone above the Red Raiders also won. Both BYU and Texas Tech have one relatively bad loss, but BYU's was by a closer score, and the Cougars have a win over Notre Dame. Wake Forest stays put after a 49-7 demolition of SMU. Similar to Texas Tech, everyone else winning prevented the Demon Deacons from climbing. There is a large gap between here and what comes next.
 Advertisement
 That next is No. 13 Oregon , which floats around CFP contention thanks to its wins over Ohio State and USC. The Ducks are ahead of No. 14 Iowa because of those wins (both beat Northwestern). USC stays put because of its win over Ohio State and because of how many teams in this range also lost.
 That includes Arizona , which is in the unusual position of moving up four spots after a one-point loss to Utah. If we're going to excuse good losses for SEC teams, that also applies to Arizona, whose three losses have come to BYU, Texas Tech and Utah by a total of 20 points. Again, so many teams lost in this range that it leads to some strange results.
 The rest of the top 25 is made up of South Carolina , which has a blowout win over Oklahoma , which has a recent win over Florida , which blew out Ole Miss , which has wins over Louisville and LSU . The Gamecocks' lopsided loss to Arkansas was bad, but we can provide some grace because quarterback LaNorris Sellers didn't play and earlier wins over Oklahoma, Tennessee and Florida all got better this weekend.
 Ultimately, a ranking is relative to what happens to all the teams around a given team. And when almost everyone loses, things can get weird.
 The carnage continues in this group. LSU falls after a last-second loss to Texas, the Tigers' third loss that came down to the final possession. Duke drops one spot after the loss to Miami. Missouri falls after a blowout loss to Georgia.
 Advertisement
 UTSA and Memphis now sit just outside the top 30 after big conference wins. New Mexico slips after a home loss to UNLV (a team Memphis beat). Other Group of 6 teams also climbed into the back of this group, including Liberty , Toledo , Western Michigan , Louisiana Tech and North Dakota State . It's the point in the year when I give teams that have a lot of wins the nod over a bunch of .500 Power 4 teams.
 Clemson also tumbles after a 20-6 loss to a Georgia Tech team that has just three wins this year.
 Stanford jumps up after beating Virginia Tech 40-22. The Cardinal's five losses are all to teams with at least seven wins. West Virginia and Cincinnati also drop into the 60s after lopsided losses to Kansas and Iowa State, respectively.
 Texas A&M slides down to No. 68 after a fourth consecutive FBS loss, but the Aggies stay ahead of rising Arkansas due to their head-to-head result. Colorado jumps up after beating Houston in the biggest upset of the weekend.
 James Madison has lost three of four since a 7-0 start and is down to No. 70 after a 46-22 loss to UConn. Tulsa moves up after beating Florida Atlantic to get bowl-eligible.
 UNLV moves up for beating New Mexico. Georgia Tech has wins over Duke and Clemson but losses to Boston College, Stanford and Pittsburgh's backup quarterback; it's been a strange year, and staff changes are already underway. Michigan State , NC State and Purdue slip down after losses.
 Georgia Southern is atop the Sun Belt East after beating Georgia State. Miami (Ohio) bounces back up to No. 91 after beating rival Ohio , which moves down to No. 94.
 Advertisement
 Cal tumbles after a blowout loss at Virginia, its fourth consecutive loss by at least 21 points. UAB beat Temple to get bowl-eligible in Alex Mortensen's first full season as head coach.
 Fresno State and Georgia State fall out of the top 100 after losses. Rutgers is down to No. 104, the lowest Power 4 team, after getting shut out by Nebraska.
 Western Kentucky moves up after an upset of Jacksonville State. Missouri State beat New Mexico State in overtime with a walk-off pick six and moves up to No. 119. Washington State destroyed Colorado State 73-7, moving the Cougars past the Rams. Colorado State has one of the worst defenses in modern college football history.
 Bowling Green beat Kent State to move up to No. 129. Charlotte has been competitive enough in recent weeks to slide up one spot to No. 136. No. 138 Northern Illinois remains winless after a 28-7 loss to Nevada.
